items.title: Absolute, Sovereign, Almighty Love
items.summary: God does not need us. Instead, his infinite self-sufficiency spills over in love to us who need him.

items.title: God Isn’t Gloomy
items.summary: If none of God’s purposes can be frustrated, then he must be the happiest of all beings.

items.title: The All-Satisfying Object
items.summary: The quest for joy is not optional, but commanded.

items.title: The Most Liberating Discovery
items.summary: Joy is not a mere option alongside worship. It is an essential component of worship.

items.title: Make War with Unbelief
items.summary: Take up the Bible, ask the Holy Spirit for help, lay the promises up in your heart, and fight the good fight — to live by faith in future grace.

items.title: Our Good Is His Glory
items.summary: God’s greatest interest is to glorify the wealth of his grace by making sinners happy in him.

items.title: The Power of a Superior Promise
items.summary: The truth of Christ frees us from the slavery of sin, for the freedom of holiness.

items.title: The Gospel Before Jesus Died
items.summary: Did Jesus preach the gospel before his death and resurrection? Pastor John calls us to a deeper understanding of God as Creator and King, and Jesus as Lord and Savior.

items.title: The Perils of a Quick Fix
items.summary: How can we witness to those who just want a quick fix? Pastor John presses home the shocking reality of eternity and the astounding love of Jesus.

items.title: When I’m Too Weak to Be Productive
items.summary: Can a disabled mother model the Proverbs 31 woman? Pastor John describes the gift of a heart that hopes in God’s steadfast love.

items.title: Six Traits of a Forgettable Sermon
items.summary: Rigorous exposition isn’t at odds with engaging preaching. Pastor John encourages pastors to work for creativity when technical, abstract sermons feel easier.

items.title: Do We Need to Go to Church Every Week?
items.summary: Gathering with other Christians is a crucial way to encourage and be encouraged in Christ. But do we really need to gather every week?

items.title: The Joy That Sustained Jesus
items.summary: Jesus endured unspeakable agony at the cross. Pastor John marvels at the force of his love sustained by expectant joy.

items.title: Love and the Practical Graces
items.summary: The city of Corinth was a place of commerce. Nobody went there except to be successful. It was built from scratch just a few decades before Paul’s letter was written. There were not old families and traditions. This was a place that attracted an unusually resourceful, talented, ambitious, intense kind of person. And…

items.title: Paul’s Detour
items.summary: As we find ourselves discouraged with our circumstances in life, we usually react in one of three ways. We might harden ourselves by saying life is unfair and we should get used to it, we might be overcome by despair, or we might simply believe everything will get better for us soon. The apostle Paul shows us there’s…

items.title: Politics of the Kingdom
items.summary: We sometimes think becoming a Christian is something that has to take a lot of time and effort. As we consider what we believe, it can be easy to feel as if we’re somewhere between “not a believer” and “someone saved by Christ.” But the Bible gives us a different interpretation: we are either strangers to this world…

items.title: Spiritual Maturity
items.summary: Facing hardship allows us to deepen our reliance on God.

items.title: Avoiding Compromise
items.summary: God's Word is our safeguard against the temptation to compromise, leading us on the path of His will.

items.title: When Compromise Creeps In
items.summary: Sin has a way of pulling us farther than we planned, but no believer is beyond the reach of God's grace.

items.title: Faithful With What He's Given
items.summary: Being a good steward means taking what God has given you and investing it in His kingdom.

items.title: A Partner for Accountability
items.summary: What are the qualities we should look for in an accountability partner?

items.title: Freedom That Considers Others
items.summary: As believers, we're called to be sensitive to and considerate of those who are new to faith.

items.title: Uniting Belief and Behavior
items.summary: When genuine faith is the foundation of our belief and behavior, it becomes noticeable to those around us.

items.title: The Seriousness of Sin (1 Chronicles 13:10)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 13:10, David Platt urges us to respond to sin with sober-mindedness. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Jesus Is Our Shepherd-King (1 Chronicles 11:2)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 11:2, David Platt teaches that Jesus leads, protects, and cares for his people. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Trust and Obey (1 Chronicles 10:13–14)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 10:13–14, David Platt encourages us to be faithful to God's commands. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Christ's Surpassing Worth (1 Chronicles 8:40)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 8:40, David Platt emphasizes the incomparable worth of knowing Jesus Christ over any worldly achievement. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Your Life for God’s Glory (1 Chronicles 7:27)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 7:27, David Platt encourages us to surrender our lives to God’s purposes. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: The Power of Worship (1 Chronicles 6:31–32)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 6:31–32, David Platt explains the spiritual significance of singing as a form of worship. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Ask Boldly (1 Chronicles 4:10)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 4:10, David Platt encourages Christians to ask God boldly and humbly for his blessing. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Your View of God Shapes Everything
items.summary: You may not deny God, but do you diminish Him? In this episode, Costi Hinn examines how a small or distorted view of God can shape the way we live, exposing the gap between what we confess about God and how we actually function day to day.

items.title: No One Is Above God
items.summary: The name El Elyon means “God Most High,” declaring God’s absolute supremacy over everyone and everything. In this final episode of the Names of God series, Costi Hinn explains what it means to live with the perspective that God is sovereign, owns everything, and answers to no one.

items.title: Why Is God Jealous?
items.summary: God’s jealousy is not sinful, insecure, or possessive. It is His holy zeal for His glory and His covenant relationship with His people. In this episode, Costi Hinn explains what it means for God to be El Qanna, the jealous God, and why He refuses to share the worship that belongs exclusively to Him.

items.title: God Is Stronger Than Your Circumstances
items.summary: In this episode, Costi Hinn explores El Gibbor, the Mighty God, and what this name reveals about the strength, sovereignty, and victory of God. When life feels bigger than you, remember: you don’t have to be strong enough. Your God is.

items.title: The God Who Sees You
items.summary: In this episode, Costi Hinn explores the name El Roi—the God who sees me. Through the story of Hagar, we’re reminded that God sees us in our pain, our struggles, and the moments when everyone else overlooks us. But His seeing also means He sees our sin, our motives, and our private lives. El Roi brings both comfort…
